checks: Difficulty-dependent candidate counts, canonical affixes, diversity and deterministic redisplay across 576 constructed batches
Final action saved before return settlement recovers one identical offer and settlement
Offer display changes neither inventory nor funds nor active game random state
A successful purchase atomically spends only unspent funds and adds one exact acquired item
Insufficient unspent funds cannot silently refund learned bases or partially purchase
Second purchase, conflicting operation, stale candidate and reserved object-key operation fail unchanged
Purchased passive obeys learned-base and total equipment cost gates; an equipped copy cannot be sold
Free relearning refunds actual base fees, keeps purchases and fractions, and does not refund acquisition spending
Immediate conversion loses 3.5 points and purchase replay after sale never recreates an item
Purchased cards materialize their exact variant without a new saleable possession
Saved offer or price modification is rejected; replay and free respec keep the offer
Buying while exploring fails without changing the session
A retained easy completion inside C does not earn unretained higher-difficulty candidates
Defeat and empty withdrawal do not refresh; effort and low HP do not raise difficulty
Only a new retained-completion return refreshes the batch; earlier unbought candidates cannot be purchased
A later return may sell the identical performance again as a distinct acquired copy
